q: The section modulus of a rectangular section is proportional to
options: square of the area of the section
half moment of inertia of the section
explanation: Z = bd²/6 for a rectangular section — it scales with the section's area and depth together.

q: Find the maximum BM induced in a cantilever beam subjected to a point load of 10 KN. Length of beam is 10 m. The load is located at a distance of 3 m from the free end:-
explanation: Distance from the fixed end = 10 − 3 = 7 m. M = 10 × 7 = 70 kN-m.

q: Find the maximum SF induced in a cantilever beam subjected to a point load of 10 KN. Length of beam is 10 m. The load is located at a distance of 3 m from the free end
explanation: For a single point load on a cantilever, the shear force between the fixed end and the load point equals the load itself, 10 kN.

q: The reaction at end A of the beam shown (UDL of 2 kN/m over a beam with overhangs of l/2 on each side of a central support arrangement) is
explanation: Based on the symmetric overhang/support arrangement shown in the figure, the reaction at A works out to zero.

q: Find the bending moment at center and also find the maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam of span 5 m with a 10 KN point load located 2 m from one support and 3 m from the other
explanation: RA = 10×3/5 = 6 kN. BM at load point (max) = 6×2 = 12 kN-m. BM at center (2.5 m from A) = 6×2.5 − 10×0.5 = 10 kN-m.

q: A cantilever beam of span 4 m and carrying a point load of 10 KN located at 3 m from the fixed end. Find the BM at the fixed and free end
explanation: BM at fixed end = 10×3 = 30 kN-m; BM at the free end of any cantilever is always zero.

q: The maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam is where the UDL is applied
explanation: Under a full-span UDL, maximum BM occurs at mid-span.

q: The maximum BM produced in a simply supported beam having span 4 m and subjected to a UDL of 10 kN/m
explanation: M_max = wL²/8 = 10×4²/8 = 20 kN-m.

q: A long vertical member subjected to an axial compressive load is called
explanation: A long vertical compression member is classically termed a column.

q: A column that fails primarily due to direct stress is called
explanation: Short columns fail by crushing (direct compressive stress) rather than buckling.

q: A column that fails primarily due to buckling is known as
explanation: Long, slender columns fail by lateral buckling well before reaching the crushing stress.

q: Buckling load for a given column depends upon
options: both length and least lateral dimension
explanation: Euler's buckling load depends on slenderness ratio, which combines both effective length and the section's least radius of gyration (lateral dimension).

q: The effective length of a column if both ends are hinged
explanation: Both-ends-hinged is the reference case: effective length Le = L.

q: The region of c/s of a column in which compressive load may be applied without producing tensile load is known as
explanation: This region is the 'core' or 'kern' of the section — loads applied within it produce no tensile stress anywhere on the section.

q: For keeping the stress wholly compressive, the load may be applied on a circular column anywhere within a concentric circle of diameter
explanation: The kern of a solid circular section of diameter d is a concentric circle of diameter d/4.

q: In a rectangular column having cross section b × h, the core is
options: rectangle of lengths b/2 and h/2
rhombus of diagonals b/3 and h/3
explanation: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook result for a rectangular section's kern is a rhombus with diagonals b/3 and h/3 — worth double-checking against your source book, as option (d) is the classically expected answer).

q: For a column with both ends fixed, the crippling load will be equal to
explanation: Both-ends-fixed Euler load is 4× the both-ends-hinged reference load P.

q: The crippling load for a column with both ends hinged is
explanation: Standard Euler formula for the pinned-pinned reference case: Pcr = π²EI/L².

q: Euler's formula for a column of length l, with one end fixed and other hinged is
explanation: Standard result (approximate factor of 2): fixed-hinged Euler load ≈ 2π²EI/L².

q: The crippling load for column of length l, with one end fixed and the other end free is
explanation: Standard Euler formula for a fixed-free column: Pcr = π²EI/4L².

q: The value of buckling load is ___ than crushing load in case of long column
explanation: For long, slender columns, the Euler buckling load is reached well before the crushing (yield) load — that's precisely why long columns fail by buckling first.

q: The effective length of a column effectively held in position and restrained in direction at one end will be
explanation: As per the standard end-condition tables for this specific restraint case.

q: Effective length of a column fixed at one end and hinged at the other end is
explanation: Standard result: fixed-hinged effective length Le = L/√2 ≈ 0.707L.

q: The equivalent length of a column fixed at one end and free at the other end, is
explanation: Standard result: fixed-free (cantilever) effective length Le = 2L.

q: The ratio of the effective length of a column and minimum radius of gyration of its cross-sectional area, is known as
explanation: Slenderness ratio λ = Le/k_min, by definition.

q: For a column of given material, the Rankine's constant depends on
explanation: Rankine's constant (1/a = σc/π²E) depends only on the material's crushing stress and modulus of elasticity — not on the column's length, diameter, or moment of inertia.

q: A truss is completely analyzed, when
options: the direct stress in all the members are found
all the external reactions components are determined
explanation: A truss analysis is complete once the axial (direct) force/stress in every member has been determined.

q: Strut is a
explanation: A strut is defined by its function (carrying compression), not its orientation — it may be horizontal, vertical, or inclined.

q: A tie is a member which
options: is subjected to axial compression only
is subjected to axial tension only
is subjected to moment tension only
is subjected to two equal and opposite forces
explanation: A tie carries axial tension only, as opposed to a strut which carries compression.

q: The maximum bending moment in a simply supported beam loaded with a UDL of w/m having span l is
explanation: Standard formula: M_max = wl²/8 for a full-span UDL on a simply supported beam.
